findings.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) can silently win provider selection when no other provider is present, but then nearly every method throws an unhelpful UnsupportedOperationException instead of a clear 'provider missing' error; previously CryptoIntegration threw IllegalStateException ('Not able to load any cryptoProvider'), so callers relying on that failure signal get obscure UOE later

CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now silently picks the highest-order provider and only logs ignored ones at DEBUG, removing the previous hard failure on multiple providers; ServiceLoader iteration order among equal-order providers (e.g. DefaultCryptoProvider and WildFlyElytronProvider both = 200) is classpath-dependent, so which provider wins is undefined — a FIPS-required deployment could non-deterministically get the non-FIPS provider with no error/warning

CryptoIntegration.init is only called from AuthzClient.create(Configuration); AuthzClient instances constructed via other paths (serialization, direct construction, other entry points) never initialize the crypto integration, and CryptoIntegration.getProvider() throws only if never init'd. Additionally, the new service file in authz-client means any app with authz-client alongside another CryptoProvider now has two providers, silently changing which provider serves the whole JVM

Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two unused encoder objects are created and discarded (ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);), suggesting an editing mistake with no functional impact

ASN1Decoder.readLength() bound check compares length against the global limit instead of bytes remaining after tag/length octets, so a nested TLV can declare a length that overruns the stream and only fails later in read() with a less specific EOF error rather than being rejected at length parse

ASN1Decoder.mark() uses is.available() as mark limit and readNext()'s length += reset() assumes count only counts bytes since the mark — correct here but the pattern breaks if the underlying stream type ever changes

ASN1Decoder.readNext() (~line 82): if readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80), length += reset() yields a negative value and read(length) does new byte[negative], causing an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException that escapes IOException handling when parsing attacker-controlled DER signature input

ASN1Decoder.readSequence() (~line 55): length = length - bytes.length subtracts only the content length but length was the full TLV length including tag/header bytes, causing the loop to underflow/overshoot on crafted input, throwing unexpected exceptions or mis-parsing

ASN1Decoder.readLength() bounds check uses length >= limit where limit is the total buffer size instead of the bytes remaining at the current position, allowing a valid-looking early element to declare a length extending past remaining data (only caught later by the EOF check in read())

CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (~lines 53-70): silently picks the highest order() provider and only logs at debug level that others were 'Ignored', replacing the previous fail-closed hard error on multiple CryptoProvider implementations with fail-open behavior — a misassigned provider (e.g., in FIPS deployments) could silently win

AuthzClient.create() (~line 95) can re-initialize the JVM-wide cached crypto provider in CryptoIntegration with the client's classloader, potentially swapping a FIPS-enabled provider with the limited AuthzClientCryptoProvider, weakening crypto used elsewhere in the process

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() (~line 52) returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the JKS/PKCS12 provider (e.g., SUN) rather than a BC-equivalent provider — callers relying on it for algorithm availability (e.g., EC, PSS) may silently get a provider that lacks those algorithms

AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered globally via META-INF/services with order(100) but only supports ECDSA signature conversion and stubs everything else with UnsupportedOperationException, so any component using CryptoIntegration in a classloader that sees the authz-client jar may fail at runtime with an unclear error instead of failing at discovery time

Dead allocations in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`: the first two `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls build encoders whose output is discarded, doing ~2x the necessary work on the token-signature-verification hot path; delete the first two lines
`AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` triggers `CryptoIntegration.init` (ServiceLoader classpath scan) on every call; should initialize once since the provider set cannot change within a JVM

`ASN1Decoder.readSequence` returns an empty list for indefinite-length (0x80) encodings because length == -1 makes the `while (length > 0)` loop never execute, silently producing an empty sequence instead of an error

`ASN1Decoder.readLength` bounds check compares against the total input size rather than bytes remaining, so a declared length near the end of the stream can pass validation and still throw later in `read()`

ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length DER input, but read(int) calls new byte[-1], throwing unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of the declared IOException, so malformed JWT signatures surface as uncaught runtime exceptions

In readSequence(), an indefinite-length (-1) value makes the while (length > 0) loop silently produce an empty list rather than an error; indefinite-length should be explicitly rejected (invalid in DER) or handled

CryptoIntegration.detectProvider silently picks the highest order() provider instead of failing fast on multiple providers, and ties (DefaultCryptoProvider=200, WildFlyElytronProvider=200, FIPS1402Provider=200) fall back to nondeterministic ServiceLoader classpath order

Equal-order ambiguity between providers with materially different behavior (FIPS vs non-FIPS) is logged at debug rather than warn/error, so picking the wrong provider causes later runtime failures with no diagnostic

AuthzClientCryptoProvider registers itself globally via SPI in META-INF/services despite order()=100, so applications embedding the authz-client jar get a partial provider whose methods throw UnsupportedOperationException

AuthzClient.create() re-invokes CryptoIntegration.init() on every call, which could replace a correctly-initialized provider (e.g., FIPS in a Keycloak server sharing the same classloader) depending on init()'s caching semantics

ASN1Decoder.readLength() checks length against the limit of the entire input rather than the remaining bytes of the enclosing sequence, allowing nested TLVs to declare lengths that overrun their parent sequence
readSequence() never validates that the sum of children exactly consumes the declared sequence length, so malformed/adversarial signature encodings can be accepted or parsed inconsistently

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default JCA keystore provider (typically SunJCE/Sun) under a method contract callers interpret as the BC provider, causing late, confusing failures

ECDSA test in ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:57-60 only verifies a self-roundtrip (asn1derToConcatenatedRS → concatenatedRSToASN1DER → asn1derToConcatenatedRS), which is a tautology that cannot catch malformed DER output; no verification against an independent implementation like Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA")
concatenatedRSToASN1DER contains dead code (ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) / .write(sBigInteger) results discarded) that the roundtrip test cannot catch

Behavioral change in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (CryptoIntegration.java:57-63) from throwing IllegalStateException on multiple providers to silently selecting the highest-order() provider has no test coverage
Ordering tie-breaking when both DefaultCryptoProvider and WildFlyElytronProvider return order() == 200 is unspecified by the Comparator and untested
No test verifies that the higher-order provider wins in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, nor that the previous multiple-providers error path regression is gone

No integration test that the new META-INF/services file plus CryptoIntegration.init in AuthzClient.create works end-to-end via ServiceLoader discovery (ECDSAAlgorithmTest instantiates AuthzClientCryptoProvider directly)
No test asserts CryptoIntegration.getProvider() instanceof AuthzClientCryptoProvider in the authz-client test environment, nor covers the classpath-shadowing precedence scenario

No malformed-input or edge-case tests for the hand-rolled ASN1Decoder, whose error paths (invalid tag, high tag numbers, >4-byte lengths, out-of-bounds lengths, indefinite-length returning -1 silently treated as empty in readSequence, EOF conditions) are untested

concatenatedRSToASN1DER leading-sign handling (integerToBytes truncation branch and sign-byte handling for leading zero bytes) in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:88-100 is untested for edge values; only hit incidentally by three random signatures, needing explicit known r/s test vectors
Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements discard their results and have no effect; should be deleted (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java ~112-115)

Duplicated ECDSA ASN.1/concat conversion logic: AuthzClientCryptoProvider reimplements asn1derToConcatenatedRS/concatenatedRSToASN1DER already existing in DefaultCryptoProvider; ~3 copies of subtle crypto-format code maintained; should be extracted to a shared module

Silently swallowing multiple crypto providers in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: replaces fail-fast IllegalStateException with silent selection by order(), ignored providers logged only at debug level, deferring failures to confusing UnsupportedOperationException and potentially masking FIPS downgrade; should at least log WARN of selected provider

Half-stubbed provider shipped via ServiceLoader: 15 of ~20 CryptoProvider methods in AuthzClientCryptoProvider throw UnsupportedOperationException but registered in META-INF/services, causing runtime failures with no compile/load-time indication; hidden coupling to which methods authz-client uses

Misleading getBouncyCastleProvider(): returns the JDK default keystore provider (KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()), not a BouncyCastle provider; should throw UnsupportedOperationException if unneeded or be fixed if needed

Repeated CryptoIntegration.init() on every AuthzClient.create() call: initialization logic embedded in a per-call factory method instead of a static initializer or lifecycle hook; placement is fragile

Fragile mark/reset bookkeeping in ASN1Decoder: maintains its own count field duplicating stream position tracking, and mark(is.available()) silently depends on the stream being a ByteArrayInputStream; should use a single source of truth for position

CryptoIntegration no longer fails fast on multiple crypto providers; ties (order()==200 among DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) are resolved nondeterministically by ServiceLoader iteration order
Silent FIPS downgrade: if a non-FIPS provider leaks onto the classpath in a FIPS deployment, the server may silently run with the non-FIPS provider, logging only at DEBUG

getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JCA default keystore provider (typically SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, causing NoSuchAlgorithmException/NoSuchProviderException or unexpected crypto behavior if shared code uses it

CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration); other construction paths (create(), direct new AuthzClient(...)) skip initialization and fail later at token validation with IllegalStateException; repeated create() with different classloaders has stale cached provider hazard

ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks round-trip stability (asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x), which cannot catch encoder bugs; should assert re-encoded DER equals original sign bytes and passes Signature.verify

ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts negative INTEGERs via new BigInteger(bytes) without validation, and integerToBytes silently truncates/pads two's-complement bytes; readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length (0x80) encodings
Dead computation in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and their output discarded, obscuring the intended encoding

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) can silently win provider selection when no other provider is present, but then nearly every method throws an unhelpful UnsupportedOperationException instead of a clear 'provider missing' error; previously CryptoIntegration threw IllegalStateException ('Not able to load any cryptoProvider'), so callers relying on that failure signal get obscure UOE later

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SPI crypto provider for authz-client (META-INF/services/...CryptoProvider -> AuthzClientCryptoProvider) and makes AuthzClient.create() call CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()), so CryptoIntegration will now successfully detect a provider in authz-client instead of failing fast due to “no cryptoProvider”. AuthzClientCryptoProvider implements order()=100 but most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException (e.g., getPemUtils/getCertificateUtils/getSignature/etc.), so any downstream use of those APIs will now fail later with UOE rather than an immediate “missing provider” IllegalStateException. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about error signaling/completeness of the provider, but the diff doesn’t prove those unsupported methods are actually invoked in the affected runtime paths, so it’s not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` was added only in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` (so initialization is tied to that factory path). Separately, the authz-client module now contributes a `CryptoProvider` via `META-INF/services/...CryptoProvider`, and `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` was changed to no longer throw on multiple providers; instead it sorts by `CryptoProvider.order()` and silently selects the highest-order provider while only debug-logging ignored ones. That combination creates a real, diff-grounded integration/architecture concern about global provider selection behavior when authz-client is on the classpath with other providers. Claims about other construction paths (serialization/direct construction/other entry points) and exact `getProvider()` throwing behavior aren’t fully verifiable from the shown diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two unused encoder objects are created and discarded (ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);), suggesting an editing mistake with no functional impact

ASN1Decoder.readLength() bound check compares length against the global limit instead of bytes remaining after tag/length octets, so a nested TLV can declare a length that overruns the stream and only fails later in read() with a less specific EOF error rather than being rejected at length parse

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the out-of-bounds check uses `if (length >= limit)` where `limit` is the total input size (`bytes.length`), not the remaining bytes after already consuming tag/length octets (`count`). Since `count` is incremented by `read()` during tag/length parsing, a TLV can specify a `length` that is < `limit` but > remaining bytes, passing the check and only failing later in `read(int)` with a generic EOF IOException. This matches the finding: the bound check should be against remaining bytes, not the global limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.mark() uses is.available() as mark limit and readNext()'s length += reset() assumes count only counts bytes since the mark — correct here but the pattern breaks if the underlying stream type ever changes

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, ASN1Decoder is explicitly backed by a final ByteArrayInputStream created from a byte[] in the constructor (no alternate stream types). Using is.available() as the mark readAheadLimit is harmless for ByteArrayInputStream (reset is always supported and the limit is effectively irrelevant). The critique about the pattern breaking if the underlying stream type changes is speculative and not applicable to the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence() (~line 55): length = length - bytes.length subtracts only the content length but length was the full TLV length including tag/header bytes, causing the loop to underflow/overshoot on crafted input, throwing unexpected exceptions or mis-parsing

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the `length` value comes from `readLength()`, which per its implementation returns the ASN.1 value/content length (it reads the length octets and returns the decoded length), not the full TLV size. The outer SEQUENCE content consists of concatenated inner TLVs (including each inner tag+length+value), and `readNext()` explicitly returns the full TLV bytes by adding the header size (`length += reset()`). Therefore subtracting `bytes.length` (full inner TLV length) from the remaining outer content length is correct; the finding incorrectly assumes `length` already included tag/header bytes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() bounds check uses length >= limit where limit is the total buffer size instead of the bytes remaining at the current position, allowing a valid-looking early element to declare a length extending past remaining data (only caught later by the EOF check in read())

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the bounds check `if (length >= limit)` uses `limit = bytes.length` (total buffer size) and ignores how many bytes have already been consumed from the stream (tracked via `count`). This permits an element parsed later in the buffer to declare a length that is <= total buffer size but > remaining bytes, which then triggers failure only in `read(int length)` via EOF after allocating `new byte[length]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (~lines 53-70): silently picks the highest order() provider and only logs at debug level that others were 'Ignored', replacing the previous fail-closed hard error on multiple CryptoProvider implementations with fail-open behavior — a misassigned provider (e.g., in FIPS deployments) could silently win

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are present. It now sorts providers by order() (descending) and returns the first, only emitting a debug log listing “Ignored crypto providers” (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). This is a fail-open behavior change from the previous fail-closed exception, and can silently select an unintended provider. The risk is amplified because multiple built-in providers are assigned the same order=200 (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider), so selection among them is not clearly deterministic from the diff and may pick the wrong one without an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClient.create() (~line 95) can re-initialize the JVM-wide cached crypto provider in CryptoIntegration with the client's classloader, potentially swapping a FIPS-enabled provider with the limited AuthzClientCryptoProvider, weakening crypto used elsewhere in the process

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global initialization call in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` (`CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());`). `CryptoIntegration` appears to select and cache a `CryptoProvider` via `ServiceLoader` (see `detectProvider(ClassLoader)`), so invoking `init` from a library entrypoint can couple the whole process’s crypto-provider selection to the authz-client classloader. While the diff also introduces provider ordering and sorts providers by `order()` (making it less likely that `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (order 100) would override default/FIPS providers (order 200) when both are visible), the architectural concern remains: this call can affect JVM-wide provider selection, and the diff does not show any guard that prevents re-initialization or prevents changing an already-selected provider.

That provider implements only `getEcdsaCryptoProvider()` (and `getKeyStore()`/`getBouncyCastleProvider()`), while most required `CryptoProvider` methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. At the same time, `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` was changed to no longer fail when multiple providers exist, and will select the highest `order()`; if the authz-client jar is the only visible provider in a given classloader, discovery will succeed and later calls to unsupported methods will fail at runtime rather than failing early at discovery time. This runtime-failure risk is directly grounded in the new provider + service registration + detection behavior in the diff.

However, the finding’s key claim—that this will trigger a ServiceLoader classpath scan on every call—is not verifiable from the provided diff because the implementation of `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` and its caching/idempotence behavior is not shown. The only CryptoIntegration change shown is in `detectProvider(...)` (sorting/selection), not when/how often detection runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ASN1Decoder.readSequence` returns an empty list for indefinite-length (0x80) encodings because length == -1 makes the `while (length > 0)` loop never execute, silently producing an empty sequence instead of an error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder`, `readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`length == 0x80`). `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()` then does `while (length > 0) { ... }`, so with `length == -1` the loop never runs and the method returns an empty `List<byte[]>` without throwing, despite having consumed the SEQUENCE tag/length. This matches the finding: indefinite-length sequences are silently treated as empty rather than rejected/parsed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `ASN1Decoder.readLength` bounds check compares against the total input size rather than bytes remaining, so a declared length near the end of the stream can pass validation and still throw later in `read()`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ASN1Decoder.readLength()`, the bounds check uses `if (length >= limit)` where `limit` is the total input size (`bytes.length`), not the remaining unread bytes. Since `count` tracks how many bytes have already been consumed, a length that exceeds remaining data (but is still < total size) will pass validation and then fail later in `read(int length)` with an EOF exception. This matches the finding and is a correctness defect in the added decoder logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length DER input, but read(int) calls new byte[-1], throwing unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of the declared IOException, so malformed JWT signatures surface as uncaught runtime exceptions

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder`, `readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`length == 0x80`). Callers like `readInteger()` and `readNext()` then pass that value to `read(int length)`, which does `new byte[length]`. With `length == -1`, this throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException`, not the declared `IOException`. This is directly verifiable from the added code and means malformed/indefinite-length ASN.1 input can surface as an uncaught runtime exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In readSequence(), an indefinite-length (-1) value makes the while (length > 0) loop silently produce an empty list rather than an error; indefinite-length should be explicitly rejected (invalid in DER) or handled

adjudication.rationale: ASN1Decoder.readLength() can return -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80), and readSequence() uses `while (length > 0)` so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE yields an empty `List<byte[]>` without throwing at that point. In current diff usage (ECDSACryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS), this will later fail via `if (seq.size() != 2) throw`, so it’s not a silent acceptance end-to-end for that path, but the decoder itself doesn’t explicitly reject/handle indefinite-length (invalid for DER) as the finding notes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider silently picks the highest order() provider instead of failing fast on multiple providers, and ties (DefaultCryptoProvider=200, WildFlyElytronProvider=200, FIPS1402Provider=200) fall back to nondeterministic ServiceLoader classpath order

adjudication.rationale: In common/CryptoIntegration.detectProvider the diff changes behavior from throwing when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found to sorting by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returning foundProviders.get(0), merely logging the rest as “Ignored” (removed the previous IllegalStateException branch). The diff also sets order()=200 for DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider, so ties are possible; with equal order values, the chosen provider depends on ServiceLoader encounter order (classpath/provider-file order), which is not guaranteed to be deterministic across environments. This can lead to selecting an unintended provider instead of failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Equal-order ambiguity between providers with materially different behavior (FIPS vs non-FIPS) is logged at debug rather than warn/error, so picking the wrong provider causes later runtime failures with no diagnostic

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are present; instead it sorts by order and returns the first, only logging ignored providers at DEBUG. Multiple materially different providers now share the same order=200 (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider), and the comparator has no tie-breaker, so selection among equal-order providers is effectively dependent on ServiceLoader iteration order. This can silently pick an unintended provider (e.g., FIPS vs non-FIPS) and the only diagnostic is a DEBUG log, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider registers itself globally via SPI in META-INF/services despite order()=100, so applications embedding the authz-client jar get a partial provider whose methods throw UnsupportedOperationException

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an SPI entry `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` pointing to `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, and that provider implements `CryptoProvider` with many methods throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `getSignature`, `getPemUtils`, `getAesGcmCipher`, etc.). If an application’s classpath contains only the authz-client (or no other `CryptoProvider` implementations), `CryptoIntegration` will select this provider (it now sorts by `order()` and picks the first), and any use of unsupported methods would fail at runtime. However, the finding’s claim that this happens “despite order()=100” as a general problem is overstated: other providers in the diff have `order()=200` and will be preferred when present, so this mainly represents a potential integration/architecture risk rather than a clearly verifiable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClient.create() re-invokes CryptoIntegration.init() on every call, which could replace a correctly-initialized provider (e.g., FIPS in a Keycloak server sharing the same classloader) depending on init()'s caching semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` inside `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`, so it will run on every `create()` call. However, the diff does not show `CryptoIntegration.init()`’s caching/idempotency semantics, so it’s not verifiable from this PR that repeated init would actually replace an already-correct provider (e.g., FIPS). What *is* diff-grounded is the new repeated global initialization call, which is an architectural/scope concern if `init()` mutates shared static state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readLength() checks length against the limit of the entire input rather than the remaining bytes of the enclosing sequence, allowing nested TLVs to declare lengths that overrun their parent sequence

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the bounds check uses `if (length >= limit)` where `limit` is the total input size (`bytes.length` set in the constructor), not the remaining bytes within the currently parsed enclosing TLV/sequence. In `readSequence()`, the outer SEQUENCE length is tracked in a local `length` variable, but `readNext()`/`readLength()` do not validate that a nested element’s declared length fits within that remaining outer length. As a result, a nested TLV can declare a length larger than the remaining bytes of the outer sequence (but still < total input), causing `readNext()` to consume bytes belonging to subsequent elements or trailing data; `readSequence()` will then just subtract `bytes.length` and may end with a negative `length` without throwing. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: readSequence() never validates that the sum of children exactly consumes the declared sequence length, so malformed/adversarial signature encodings can be accepted or parsed inconsistently

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()`, the loop subtracts each child’s encoded length from the declared SEQUENCE length (`length = length - bytes.length`) but never checks that the children consume **exactly** the declared length. If a child’s encoded length exceeds the remaining `length`, `length` becomes negative and the method silently returns without error. Also, `readLength()` can return `-1` for indefinite-length encoding, and `readSequence()` would then return an empty list without rejecting it. Both cases mean malformed/adversarial encodings can be accepted or parsed inconsistently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default JCA keystore provider (typically SunJCE/Sun) under a method contract callers interpret as the BC provider, causing late, confusing failures

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is the provider backing the default keystore type (typically a Sun/Oracle provider), not a BouncyCastle provider. Given the `CryptoProvider` interface method name/contract (`getBouncyCastleProvider()`), this is misleading and could cause downstream code that expects BC-specific capabilities to behave unexpectedly if this provider is selected. The diff, however, doesn’t show a concrete call site that fails because of this, so the issue is a contract/architecture mismatch rather than a verified broken behavior in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSA test in ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:57-60 only verifies a self-roundtrip (asn1derToConcatenatedRS → concatenatedRSToASN1DER → asn1derToConcatenatedRS), which is a tautology that cannot catch malformed DER output; no verification against an independent implementation like Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA")

adjudication.rationale: In ECDSAAlgorithmTest, the test generates a DER signature using java.security.Signature, converts it to concatenated RS, converts back to DER via concatenatedRSToASN1DER, then converts that DER back to RS and asserts RS equality. This only proves the custom decoder/encoder pair are consistent with each other for that input (and that the decoder can parse a real JCA DER signature), but it does not independently validate that the DER produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER is standards-compliant (e.g., by verifying it with Signature.initVerify). So the finding about the test being limited to a self-roundtrip is accurate as a test-gap, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: concatenatedRSToASN1DER contains dead code (ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) / .write(sBigInteger) results discarded) that the roundtrip test cannot catch

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create new encoders, write to them, and then discard them without using the result. The method then correctly builds the DER sequence using new encoders inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. This is dead/unnecessary code (wasted work / misleading) but does not change behavior, so it’s not a verifiable functional bug. The roundtrip test would indeed still pass even with these redundant lines present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (CryptoIntegration.java:57-63) from throwing IllegalStateException on multiple providers to silently selecting the highest-order() provider has no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to (a) sort loaded CryptoProvider implementations by the new CryptoProvider#order() (Comparator.comparingInt(...).reversed()) and (b) no longer throw IllegalStateException when multiple providers are present; instead it returns the first (highest-order) and only logs the rest as "Ignored crypto providers". This is a nontrivial behavioral change in provider selection/ambiguity handling, and the diff does not add any test exercising the multi-provider case or validating the ordering/selection logic (the only added test is ECDSAAlgorithmTest, unrelated to detectProvider behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ordering tie-breaking when both DefaultCryptoProvider and WildFlyElytronProvider return order() == 200 is unspecified by the Comparator and untested

adjudication.rationale: In CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, providers are now sorted only by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and the first is selected; additional providers are merely logged as ignored. Several providers in the diff (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) all return order() == 200, so when more than one is present the comparator yields ties and no explicit secondary tie-breaker exists, making which provider is chosen dependent on ServiceLoader iteration/order. This is a real, diff-grounded determinism/maintainability concern (and untested), though it may not manifest if these providers are never co-present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies that the higher-order provider wins in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, nor that the previous multiple-providers error path regression is gone

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` to (a) sort providers by `CryptoProvider::order` descending and pick the first, and (b) remove the previous `foundProviders.size() > 1` hard-failure path, replacing it with debug logging of ignored providers (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). This is nontrivial selection logic/regression-sensitive behavior, but the only new test added (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) covers ECDSA signature format conversion and does not exercise provider selection or the multi-provider scenario. So the finding about missing tests for “higher-order provider wins” and “no longer errors on multiple providers” is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test that the new META-INF/services file plus CryptoIntegration.init in AuthzClient.create works end-to-end via ServiceLoader discovery (ECDSAAlgorithmTest instantiates AuthzClientCryptoProvider directly)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ServiceLoader wiring via a new `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` file pointing to `org.keycloak.authorization.client.util.crypto.AuthzClientCryptoProvider` and calls `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` inside `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. However, the only added test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) constructs `new AuthzClientCryptoProvider()` directly and never exercises `AuthzClient.create(...)` nor `CryptoIntegration`'s ServiceLoader-based detection path (`CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)`). So there is no end-to-end test verifying that the services file is packaged/loaded correctly and that `CryptoIntegration.init` discovers and selects the provider at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts CryptoIntegration.getProvider() instanceof AuthzClientCryptoProvider in the authz-client test environment, nor covers the classpath-shadowing precedence scenario

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new SPI crypto provider for authz-client (AuthzClientCryptoProvider) and registers it via META-INF/services, plus changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...) to sort providers by CryptoProvider::order and pick the highest. The only new test (ECDSAAlgorithmTest) exercises AuthzClientCryptoProvider directly but does not verify ServiceLoader/CryptoIntegration integration (no assertion that CryptoIntegration.getProvider() resolves to AuthzClientCryptoProvider in the authz-client test runtime), nor does it cover the newly introduced precedence behavior when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are on the classpath.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No malformed-input or edge-case tests for the hand-rolled ASN1Decoder, whose error paths (invalid tag, high tag numbers, >4-byte lengths, out-of-bounds lengths, indefinite-length returning -1 silently treated as empty in readSequence, EOF conditions) are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new hand-rolled parsing logic in `authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java` with multiple explicit error paths (e.g., invalid tag checks in `readSequence`/`readInteger`, high-tag-number parsing in `readTagNumber`, length parsing including `size > 4`, `length >= limit`, EOF exceptions, and `readLength` returning `-1` for indefinite-length which `readSequence` will treat as empty due to `while (length > 0)`). The only added test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) exercises a happy-path roundtrip for valid ECDSA signatures and does not cover malformed inputs or these decoder error branches. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: concatenatedRSToASN1DER leading-sign handling (integerToBytes truncation branch and sign-byte handling for leading zero bytes) in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:88-100 is untested for edge values; only hit incidentally by three random signatures, needing explicit known r/s test vectors

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial DER/concat conversion logic in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER` (prepends a leading 0 byte before `new BigInteger(r/s)`) and the reverse path’s `integerToBytes` padding/truncation (`if (qLength < bytes.length)` etc.). The only test added (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) uses three runtime-generated signatures and only asserts round-tripping, which may not deterministically exercise edge cases like when `r`/`s` require (or already include) a leading 0x00 sign byte or when `toByteArray()` produces `len+1` bytes and triggers truncation. The finding is thus a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements discard their results and have no effect; should be deleted (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java ~112-115)

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the two standalone calls `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create new encoders, write into them, and then discard them without using the resulting bytes. The method’s return value is built from a separate `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(...)` call, so those two statements have no effect and are dead/redundant code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated ECDSA ASN.1/concat conversion logic: AuthzClientCryptoProvider reimplements asn1derToConcatenatedRS/concatenatedRSToASN1DER already existing in DefaultCryptoProvider; ~3 copies of subtle crypto-format code maintained; should be extracted to a shared module

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new ECDSA signature conversion logic in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (and new `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`), but the claim that this logic is already implemented in `DefaultCryptoProvider` (and that there are “~3 copies”) is not verifiable from the provided diff: `DefaultCryptoProvider` changes only add `order()` and whitespace, and no existing ECDSA conversion code is shown for comparison. Therefore the specific “duplicated existing logic” assertion cannot be confirmed based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silently swallowing multiple crypto providers in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: replaces fail-fast IllegalStateException with silent selection by order(), ignored providers logged only at debug level, deferring failures to confusing UnsupportedOperationException and potentially masking FIPS downgrade; should at least log WARN of selected provider

adjudication.rationale: The diff in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() removes the previous fail-fast IllegalStateException when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found, and instead sorts by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returns the first provider, only logging the rest at debug level. This matches the newly introduced CryptoProvider.order() API, so it’s not inherently a defect, but it is a concrete behavior/operational concern grounded in the diff: multiple providers are now tolerated and the selection may be non-obvious (especially for equal order values, since DefaultCryptoProvider/WildFlyElytronProvider/FIPS1402Provider all return 200), and “ignored providers” visibility is limited to debug logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Half-stubbed provider shipped via ServiceLoader: 15 of ~20 CryptoProvider methods in AuthzClientCryptoProvider throw UnsupportedOperationException but registered in META-INF/services, causing runtime failures with no compile/load-time indication; hidden coupling to which methods authz-client uses

adjudication.rationale: The diff does register `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider`, and the class implements `CryptoProvider` while many methods clearly throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getSignature`, etc.). That creates a real risk of runtime failures if any code path uses those methods, with no compile/load-time signal. However, the diff does not show any concrete invocation of the unsupported methods (it appears intended mainly to supply `getEcdsaCryptoProvider()` and `getKeyStore()`), so an actual, guaranteed defect cannot be proven from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading getBouncyCastleProvider(): returns the JDK default keystore provider (KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()), not a BouncyCastle provider; should throw UnsupportedOperationException if unneeded or be fixed if needed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is the JDK keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider (and may not even be related to crypto algorithms needed elsewhere). Given the `CryptoProvider` API contract/name (“BouncyCastle provider”), this is misleading and could cause incorrect provider selection if callers use it. The diff doesn’t show any direct call path that would definitively break at runtime, so it’s best classified as a concrete API/architecture issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated CryptoIntegration.init() on every AuthzClient.create() call: initialization logic embedded in a per-call factory method instead of a static initializer or lifecycle hook; placement is fragile

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` inside `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` (AuthzClient.java), which is a factory method potentially called multiple times. From the diff alone we can verify that initialization is now performed per `create()` invocation rather than once via a static initializer or external lifecycle hook. Whether this causes incorrect behavior depends on `CryptoIntegration.init()` idempotency/performance, which is not shown here, so it’s best classified as an architecture/lifecycle concern rather than a demonstrable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile mark/reset bookkeeping in ASN1Decoder: maintains its own count field duplicating stream position tracking, and mark(is.available()) silently depends on the stream being a ByteArrayInputStream; should use a single source of truth for position

adjudication.rationale: The decoder explicitly uses a `ByteArrayInputStream` (`private final ByteArrayInputStream is;` set in the constructor), so `mark(is.available())` does not “silently depend” on some unknown stream type—it is guaranteed by the class design. The separate `count` field is intentionally used to measure how many bytes were read since `mark()` so `readNext()` can compute the total TLV length (`length += reset()`), and nothing in the diff shows this bookkeeping is incorrect or broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration no longer fails fast on multiple crypto providers; ties (order()==200 among DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) are resolved nondeterministically by ServiceLoader iteration order

adjudication.rationale: In common/CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, the code now loads all CryptoProvider implementations via ServiceLoader, sorts them by CryptoProvider::order descending, and returns foundProviders.get(0) even when multiple providers are present (it no longer throws when size > 1). In this diff, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same order() value (200), so the sort comparator treats them as equal. That means which provider ends up at index 0 depends on the ServiceLoader iteration/encounter order, which can vary with classpath/service file ordering, making provider selection effectively nondeterministic in tie cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent FIPS downgrade: if a non-FIPS provider leaks onto the classpath in a FIPS deployment, the server may silently run with the non-FIPS provider, logging only at DEBUG

adjudication.rationale: In `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` the diff removes the hard failure when multiple `CryptoProvider`s are present and instead picks the first after sorting by `CryptoProvider::order` (descending) and only logs “Ignored crypto providers” at DEBUG. In a FIPS deployment where both a FIPS provider and a non-FIPS provider are on the classpath (e.g., `FIPS1402Provider` and `DefaultCryptoProvider`), both now return `order() == 200`, so the selection depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and can silently choose the non-FIPS provider rather than failing fast. This matches the described “silent FIPS downgrade” risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JCA default keystore provider (typically SUN) instead of BouncyCastle, causing NoSuchAlgorithmException/NoSuchProviderException or unexpected crypto behavior if shared code uses it

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, i.e., the provider backing the JVM default keystore type (typically a SUN/Oracle provider), not a BouncyCastle provider. This contradicts the `CryptoProvider` contract (`getBouncyCastleProvider()` is explicitly for the BC provider) and can lead to incorrect provider selection when shared code calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider()`. The diff also makes `AuthzClient.create()` call `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`, so this provider can be selected (when it’s the only one on the authz-client classpath), exposing the incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration); other construction paths (create(), direct new AuthzClient(...)) skip initialization and fail later at token validation with IllegalStateException; repeated create() with different classloaders has stale cached provider hazard

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` added in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. It does not show the implementations of other construction paths (e.g., `create(InputStream)` body, any `create()` overload, or constructor visibility/usage), so we can’t verify they skip init or that token validation will fail with `IllegalStateException`. The claim about stale cached providers across different classloaders also isn’t verifiable from the shown changes (no cache/init semantics are in the diff beyond provider ordering).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks round-trip stability (asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x), which cannot catch encoder bugs; should assert re-encoded DER equals original sign bytes and passes Signature.verify

adjudication.rationale: In ECDSAAlgorithmTest, the assertion only checks rsConcat == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rsConcat)), i.e., decoder/encoder round-trip stability (see test(): sign -> rsConcat -> asn1Des -> rsConcat2 and Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)). It does not assert that the re-encoded DER (asn1Des) matches the original DER produced by Signature.sign() (sign), nor that the transformed signature verifies with Signature.verify. This is a concrete gap for the newly added ASN.1 encoder/decoder logic and could miss encoder correctness issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts negative INTEGERs via new BigInteger(bytes) without validation, and integerToBytes silently truncates/pads two's-complement bytes; readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length (0x80) encodings

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `ASN1Decoder.readInteger()` constructs `new BigInteger(bytes)` with no explicit check that the INTEGER is non-negative, and `integerToBytes()` will truncate or left-pad `BigInteger.toByteArray()` to a fixed length (see `AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider`). It also shows `readLength()` returns `-1` for indefinite-length (0x80), and `readSequence()` will then skip the `while (length > 0)` loop and return an empty list. However, in the only shown usage (`asn1derToConcatenatedRS`), an empty sequence results in an exception due to `seq.size() != 2`, and the intended inputs are DER ECDSA signatures (definite lengths, positive r/s), so this is more an input-validation/robustness edge-case concern than a clear functional defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead computation in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder instances are created and their output discarded, obscuring the intended encoding

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create encoder instances and write data, but the resulting encoders/bytes are never used. The actual returned DER sequence is built later via `writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))`, so the earlier two calls are dead work that can confuse readers and waste cycles, but do not change the returned encoding.
